strengths_deep_dive: Bayan demonstrates clear strengths in governance and operational stability. The institution maintains <cite id="1">an 87% independent board</cite> and earned top ratings for organizational culture and leadership [1]. Financially, the institution holds <cite id="1">6.7 months of working capital</cite>, providing significant resilience against operational downturns [1]. Since its founding in 2011, Bayan has successfully established dynamic master's programs in Islamic Chaplaincy, Education, and Leadership, proving its capacity to build lasting institutional infrastructure for the American Muslim community [3].
rich_narrative.summary: Bayan Islamic Graduate School is a non-sectarian institution that offers graduate-level Islamic education, developing chaplains and leaders grounded in the Islamic tradition [3]. In FY2024, the institution reported <cite id="3">$3,852,360 in annual revenue</cite>, reflecting steady growth from <cite id="3">$3,153,900 in FY2023</cite> [3]. The organization maintains <cite id="1">an 86.25/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> [1]. While the school maintains a strong academic framework and robust governance, financial efficiency remains a notable caveat. In FY2024, its filed <cite id="1">program expense ratio was 52.0%</cite>, while Charity Navigator's financial evaluation based on cash-adjusted program operations recorded <cite id="1">a 52.0% program expense ratio</cite> [1]. This places its operational spending well below the 75% sector benchmark and the peer program ratio median of 97.0%. Nevertheless, Bayan demonstrates solid organizational resiliency, retaining <cite id="1">6.7 months of working capital</cite> and strong governance structures to support its long-term educational mission [1].
